newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr ends sharply weaker on election prospects.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr ends sharply weaker on election prospects.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed sharply lower on Monday as investors acknowledged the likelihood that a Labour-led left-of-centre coalition government would emerge from Saturday's general election.

Two opinion polls published over the weekend showed support for the opposition Labour Party growing at the expense of the conservative National government. The three main centre-left parties now collectively hold the majority of support.

"The catalyst has really been the election polls out at the weekend," said a chief dealer. "I think the markets in general, but particularly the local market, feel that a Labour/left wing government is very much on the cards."
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6922/29 and at 66.20 on its Trade-Weighted Index, sharply down on its 0.6961/68 open. The Kiwi closed on Friday at 0.6989/96 and at 66.77 on the TWI.
Dealers said investors expected the currency to move lower if a centre-left coalition came to power after the October 12 election.

"While people aren't outright negative in terms of the currency, there is certainly a feeling that if that is the case, then we're likely to see some sort of weakness in the currency," said a dealer. "Where people differ is just how big that weakness will be."
Dealers said the price action of last week had also been a catalyst. The break below 0.6980 in New York late on Friday had prompted a round of stop-lossing.
"That was really a pretty negative environment for the Kiwi to start the week," the dealer said.
The Kiwi had lost ground against the Aussie and most other currencies but dealers said it was not yet clear whether a more drastic move was in store.

"I think the jury is still out as to whether this is the start of a much more significant move. Clearly, however, the client base out there, the customers are now reassessing where Kiwi is going to go this week and also post election," the chief dealer said.
"I think that there is a feeling that while it might not come off significantly, that it's going to have trouble making a lot of ground as well."
However, dealers said the Kiwi would probably plateau at its present level for at least the next 24 hours and saw it trading a 0.6910-40 range overnight.
